mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified copy of passport of each non-South African director, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if issuing state is not a Hague Convention member, consular legalization at the South African diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or incumbency and beneficial ownership extract for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry or registrar of companies in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization in non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized board resolution of each corporate shareholder authorizing the incorporation of the South African proprietary limited company and appointment of resident directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notary public in the shareholder's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential or business address for each director and UBO, being a utility bill, bank statement or lease agreement not older than three months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank, municipal authority or independent utility provider in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification and Hague Apostille; English sworn translation if issued in a foreign language

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under FICA ss. 21, 21A, 22 and 23; all UBOs, directors, prescribed officers and authorized signatories must be screened against the United Nations Consolidated List, South African Treasury targeted financial sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, and Interpol notices. Politically exposed persons, including domestic and foreign PEPs, require enhanced due diligence under FICA ss. 28E-28F; positive screening results trigger suspicious transaction reporting and beneficial ownership documentation escalation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services portal of the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (https://www.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in the Roman/Latin alphabet. Any of South Africa's eleven official languages may be used; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into romanized form for the registered statutory name. The name must be meaningful, must not be offensive, must not falsely imply a connection to a public office, and must comply with the naming content rules of s. 11 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon CIPC name refusal, the applicant may submit a reconsideration request through the CIPC e-Services portal within 10 business days of the notice of refusal. If reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may file an application with the Companies Tribunal under s. 160 of the Companies Act within 30 days of the refusal decision, seeking a determination that the name should remain registered or that CIPC's refusal be set aside. The appeal must attach the CIPC refusal notice, proof of reservation attempt, and legal argument demonstrating compliance with s. 11(2) and s. 11(3). A concurrently amended name reservation should be filed to avoid loss of priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only if it provides a genuine physical street address in South Africa at which legal process can be served; a post office box or private bag is not acceptable. For a standard-risk marine insurance surveyor undertaking, a monitored virtual office may comply with CIPC and FICA record-keeping requirements provided that electronic or physical records are accessible from South Africa and the company appoints a local person or compliance officer for service of process and regulatory contact.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but quantified at approximately 8% to 12% in the first year for a standard-risk marine surveyor; the likelihood rises to at least 25% in the presence of CIPC annual return non-compliance, SARS audit triggers, FIC supervisory interventions, or a regulatory complaint.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss 13(1), 14(1)-(6), 15(1), 19(1), 66(1) and 113; Companies Regulations, 2011, as amended; Protection of Personal Information Act, 2013 (for shareholder records); Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001 (for beneficial ownership filing)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), a juristic person established under the Companies Act, with head office at the dtic Campus, 77 Meintjies Street, Sunnyside, Pretoria
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CIPC Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (CIPC Form CoR 14.2), filed electronically through the CIPC e-Services portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Proprietary Limited company under the Companies Act, 2008. Share capital may be paid in cash, property, or services; escrow account rules do not apply under the Companies Act, but paid-up subscription funds must be banked in the company's corporate bank account once incorporation is registered.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the subscribers hereby adopt the Memorandum of Incorporation and proceed with incorporation of ZA Pty Ltd. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the issued shares of the Company be allotted and subscribed as set out in the subscriber register, and that the first directors, whose names appear in the MOI, be appointed with effect from the date of incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office be recorded in the MOI as [full address within the Republic of South Africa]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer and [Name] be appointed Financial Director, with joint authority to file the Notice of Incorporation, open bank accounts, and procure SARS registration. RESOLVED that this resolution be signed by all subscribers/directors and retained in the company's minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for reservation of the company name using CIPC e-Services under Form CoR 9.1, selecting 'ZA Pty Ltd' as the primary proposed name. Verify each proposed director's full name, date of birth, identity number or passport number, and residential address. Confirm SARS tax number availability and obtain certified copies of directors' identity documents before lodging.
required_dossiers: Certified identity copies or passport copies of each director/subscriber
SARS tax reference number confirmation for each director
Applicant's power of attorney if using an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because it is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, or if it is considered undesirable, a fresh Form CoR 9.1 must be filed within 5 business days with two alternative names. If the reservation is queried for incomplete data, correct the web-form fields and resubmit through the same CIPC transaction queue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of incorporation documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Subscribers/directors, notary public if signatories are outside South Africa, and CIPC as filing authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum of Incorporation using the prescribed template and include the company's exact name, registered office address, principal business description, share classes, authorised shares, directors' powers, and incorporation date. Execute the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) and the MOI (CoR 14.2) by all subscribers. If executed outside South Africa, an apostilled or notarially certified copy must accompany the e-filing.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate issued by CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC returns a compliance notice citing omissions in the MOI or signature pages, the documents must be rectified and re-uploaded within 10 business days using the same e-filing reference. Persistent errors require a fresh submission accompanied by a covering letter addressed to the CIPC Companies Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to CIPC e-Services, select 'Company Registration', verify the reserved name, upload the executed Notice of Incorporation and MOI, pay the prescribed registration fee by debit/credit card or eFT, and submit the application. Upon successful processing, CIPC will issue an electronic registration certificate and a company registration number. A beneficial ownership filing must also be completed on CIPC for each shareholder and director.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.2 MOI completed and signed
Proof of payment of registration fee
Beneficial ownership schedule in CIPC prescribed format
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or rejected, CIPC will issue a non-compliance notification identifying the defect. Re-submit the corrected forms within 10 business days; if the rejection relates to the name, reserve a new name under Step 1 and attach a covering note explaining the correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS tax, UIF and COIDA registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling; Department of Employment and Labour (DEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the CIPC registration certificate, register the company as a taxpayer on SARS eFiling for income tax. Mandatorily register as an employer for Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) and Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) if employees are engaged. Register for VAT if taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed R1 million per annum. Apply to the Compensation Fund for a Letter of Good Standing under COIDA using the company registration details.
required_dossiers: Company MOI and Notice of Incorporation
Bank account confirmation in the company name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS delays PIN issuance or rejects the VAT registration, use the SARS eFiling 'Request Tax Compliance Status' function and escalate to the SARS branch via an online inquiry. If the Compensation Fund returns a discrepancy in the COIDA letter, correct the company trade classification code and re-apply at the nearest DEL Labour Centre.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening, professional indemnity cover and beneficial ownership recordal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banking institution (e.g. FNB, Standard Bank, Absa, Nedbank) and CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the company name by presenting the CIPC registration certificate, MOI, board resolution, and directors' identification. Obtain a SARS tax compliance status statement for the company. Secure professional indemnity and public liability insurance for marine surveying activities, and ensure the CIPC beneficial ownership register is filed in the required format, identifying all natural persons who hold or control 5% or more shares, and all senior managing officers.
required_dossiers: First board resolution appointing account signatories
Certified copies of directors' identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account application due to missing beneficial ownership particulars, correct the shareholder register and resubmit with an updated resolution. If CIPC returns the beneficial ownership filing, amend the register online and reissue within 5 business days through the CIPC's beneficial ownership filing portal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic); South African Maritime Safety Authority (SAMSA); local municipal business licensing authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Marine Surveyor Accreditation and Insurance Claims Investigation Business Operating Registration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Registration: the company's principal services are office-based desktop surveys and physical inspection of hulls, cargo, and containers; these activities do not trigger a full Scoping/EIA under the EIA Regulations, 2014 (Listing Notices 1-3), provided no permanent physical foundations, port-side workshops, or waste-processing installations are constructed. If a leased survey workshop is set up at a port, a municipal land-use consent and DFFE registration may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater discharge is allowed unless a water use licence is granted under the National Water Act, 1998. VOC, particulate, and combustion emissions from any mobile survey generators, ultrasonic devices, or paint-testing equipment must comply with National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act, 2004, including the prescribed emission limits for controlled emitters in listed activities. Hazardous wastes such as oil-contaminated rags, damaged battery cargo, and residual petroleum samples must be stored in sealed containers and transported only by registered waste carriers under the Waste Act, 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate and evacuation plan must be approved by the local Fire and Rescue Service for the registered office and any leased port-side premises; structural load inspection is required for any area storing heavy marine survey equipment or specimen containers; compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993 requires a formal risk assessment, first-aid and incident reporting procedures, personal fall protection, and a Letter of Good Standing from the Department of Employment and Labour under the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act, 1993 before field staff undertake vessel surveys.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); online portal: SARS eFiling (https://www.sars.gov.za and https://efiling.sars.gov.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: After CIPC incorporation, the company must register on SARS eFiling to obtain an income tax reference number; the public officer (for a non-resident entity, a resident public officer) files the VAT101 new-vendor application for a VAT registration number and submits founding documents (CIPC registration, memorandum of incorporation, director/person particulars, bank confirmation). SARS issues separate income tax and VAT vendor numbers upon approval.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the (Pty) Ltd is a South African resident company taxed on worldwide income at the corporate income tax rate; no automatic pass-through to shareholders.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election is available; a South African (Pty) Ltd is compulsorily taxed as a company. Available statutory elections include small business corporation status, VAT vendor grouping, VAT voluntary registration election, and certain CFC and transfer-pricing elections. Hybrid mismatch rules operate as automatic anti-abuse countermeasures rather than taxpayer elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAT registration threshold: R1,000,000 taxable supplies in the preceding 12-month period; voluntary registration threshold: R50,000 taxable supplies. Marine survey fees are taxable supplies unless a zero-rating or exemption applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS does not currently impose a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping requirement for every invoice. VAT vendors must issue prescribed VAT tax invoices, submit VAT201 returns via eFiling, and retain full electronic audit trails; SARS e-invoicing is partly voluntary and requires compliance with SARS technical specifications if adopted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT applies under section 56(1) of the VAT Act when movable goods are supplied to a non-resident under sale/export and physically removed from South Africa within the prescribed period, with acceptable proof of export. Services: section 54 zero-rates a supply of services to a non-resident recipient where the services are not used or consumed in South Africa; a marine insurance surveying and damage-inspection service may qualify only where the service benefit is received outside South Africa and is not supplied directly in connection with movable or immovable property situated in South Africa at the time of performance.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) and bill of lading/air waybill/road manifest evidencing physical export of goods
Commercial invoice, packing list, and survey/claim report (where services are the subject of export)
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank foreign-currency receipt confirmation evidencing proceeds repatriation
Non-resident declaration/affidavit from the recipient and contract terms demonstrating offshore use or consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS will scrutinise export documentation, recipient non-residency, use/consumption, and receipt of foreign funds. Erroneous or fraudulent zero-rating is clawed back by additional VAT assessment plus understatement penalties, statutory interest, suspension of refunds and possible criminal prosecution; failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day exchange-control window attracts SARB administrative penalties and may invalidate the export zero-rating claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), administering the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933) and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961; enforcement and day-to-day transactional approvals are delegated to authorised dealers, i.e., registered South African commercial banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The rand (ZAR) is a partially convertible currency. Current-account transactions (cross-border payment for marine survey services, reinsurance premium/claim flows, director fees and dividends) are freely accessible through an authorised dealer on submission of the underlying contract/invoice and a valid SARS tax clearance certificate. Capital-account flows (inward equity subscription, shareholder loans, outward direct investment) remain subject to exchange control approval via Form A.2/A.1 or FinSurv rulings. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted only from after-tax reserves; a SARS 'good standing' tax clearance is mandatory, and a standard 20% dividend withholding tax applies unless reduced by an applicable DTA.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export proceeds derived from exported services (including marine hull/cargo claims inspection fees earned from non-resident insurers) must be brought into South Africa within 180 days from the invoice date. Upon receipt, the hard-currency amount is cleared through the authorised dealer and must be either credited in rand (effectively a 100% conversion obligation) or, if the exporter has obtained approval for a Foreign Currency Account, retained in that account while still being subject to the 180-day repatriation window. No reduced statutory surrender percentage applies to ZAR; exporters may not retain foreign exchange offshore without FinSurv consent.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Operational ZAR Account with FX/forward desk

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: FirstRand Bank Limited (FNB / Rand Merchant Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Business Transactional Account with RMB electronic FX treasury
Corporate Current Account with eXpert cross-border FX service
Corporate+ Operational Account and Trade Finance desk
Specialised Treasury and Private Bank Account (relationship-intensive)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as primary clearing rail; SUPPLEMENTARY ONLY. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) do not hold a SARB banking or authorised-dealer licence and therefore cannot open a domestic ZAR clearing account or convert currency lawfully inside South Africa. They remain viable only for (i) receipt of low-value multicurrency survey fees parked outside SA and (ii) disbursement to foreign sub-surveyors, provided the underlying funds were first repatriated/converted through a local authorised dealer. Persistent routing of company revenue through an unlicensed EMI would breach FIC Act account-monitoring obligations and exchange control rules and would erode the entity's SARS/CIPC compliance position.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permissible under the FIC Act's risk-based approach and FIC Guidance Note 7 (2021), and no absolute statutory mandate requires all directors to appear at a branch. In practice, the major SA banks require a structured digital (video) KYC interview with the compliance officer for non-resident beneficial owners, plus a notarised/apostilled board resolution and certified passports. A marine insurance surveyor (standard low-risk, licensed) can therefore open its account fully remotely through Standard Bank or RMB; however, physically attending one interim branch meeting in Johannesburg or Cape Town (one director only) accelerates the granting of the outward MT103/FX mandate and is the recommended practical step.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner(s) lacking a provable source of wealth for the initial capital subscription (inbound equity escrow).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A 24-month personal bank statement for each funding account, audited financial statements of the shareholder entity, the executed share subscription agreement, a marine survey retainer/engagement contract evidencing the lawful fee income, a certified affidavit of source of wealth, and notarised English translations of all non-English documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: CIPC beneficial-ownership mismatch, nominee shareholding or a non-transparent shell chain obscuring the ultimate natural-person controller.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed CIPC beneficial-ownership register (CoR 44.2), an up-to-date Companies Act 71 of 2008 UBO declaration, an entity-organisational chart down to the natural person, certified passports of every UBO, and, where applicable, trust deed extracts confirming the settlor/trustee/beneficiary layers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outward FX red flag: proposed remittance to a related offshore underwriter for 'consulting' without underlying inspection deliverables.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The signed claims-survey or marine insurance inspection contract, a detailed itemised invoice for the specific hull/cargo survey, evidence of performance (survey report, timestamped vessel/cargo photographs, geolocation logs and correspondence), the completed Exchange Control Form A.1 with the correct BOP services code, a valid SARS tax clearance certificate, and VAT/export-service justification under the Value-Added Tax Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank underwriting rejection because the entity's sectoral licensing is not evidenced (marine surveying is a statutory licence-required activity).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A certified copy of the sectoral licence or registration, e.g., SAMSA (South African Maritime Safety Authority) accreditation or SAAMS (South African Association of Marine Surveyors) membership, professional indemnity insurance certificate, ISIC 5222 scope statement confirming non-fund-holding inspection services only, and the Directors' Register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP screening hit on an offshore insurer client or a shareholder domiciled in a high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A sanctions-screening explanation letter, the warrant/incorporation extract of the client entity, a third-party database search (Dow Jones/World-Check clean result), a LexisNexis due-diligence report, and a ministerial/PEP declaration stating the absence of politically exposed relationships; the file is escalated for enhanced due diligence under section 21B read with section 21D of the FIC Act.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders must transmit the injected equity by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for large nostro-covered transfers) from a bank account held in the shareholder's own name; the 20x narrative field must state the company's exact name, its CIPC registration number and the descriptor 'Subscription for shares - marine insurance surveying (ISIC 5222)'. The receiving authorised dealer validates the flow, applies the BOP direct-investment code, and credits a ZAR operational account. Foreign-currency funds are automatically converted to rand at the dealing rate; a shareholder loan requires Form A.2 completion and appears as inward lending in FinSurv records. The allotment (CoR 21.2) must be filed with CIPC within 31 days of receipt. The company should retain the MT103 confirmation, the bank's foreign-exchange certificate, the board allotment resolution and the shareholder's source-of-funds dossier for regulatory audit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails are tiered by counterparty: (i) non-resident insurers, reinsurers and independent co-surveyors are paid via SWIFT MT103 through the authorised dealer using Form A.1 and BOP code 3600 (other business services) or the closest marine-survey service code; (ii) intra-group claims settlement excess-of-loss payments use MT202 COVER with a nostro account; (iii) high-value inspection contracts linked to exported/imported cargo are best supported by a documentary letter of credit (UCP600) issued by the corporate bank; (iv) SACU/SADC counterparties can be settled in rand through the country's RTGS (SAMOS) with SWIFT MT103 confirmation. Every outward payment must be supported by a SARS good-standing tax clearance, the underlying invoice, the signed contract, and proof of the service actually being performed; exchange-control audits require these records for five years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward Exchange Contract (FEC) with a SARB authorised dealer to lock in booked USD/EUR/GBP marine survey fee receivables, non-speculative and supported by invoiced export-service exposure (typically up to 12 months).
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) on ZAR/offshore currency pairs, permitted only for specific cross-border claims or capital-structure exposure with prior FinSurv/authorised-dealer approval.
Cross-currency swap matching the company's foreign-currency reinsurance claim liabilities, approved by the authorised dealer and reported to SARB under derivative exposure rules.
European-style FX options purchased for booked trade/claims flows; speculative uncovered options are prohibited under exchange control and the Financial Markets Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (AR) filing and confirmation of Company and Beneficial Ownership records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each company registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 50% of the prescribed annual fee; if annual returns remain outstanding for two consecutive years, CIPC may initiate compulsory strike-off/deregistration procedure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after accounting year-end, or on any earlier date published by SARS for the applicable corporate tax season
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative non-compliance penalty of up to 200% of assessed tax under the Tax Administration Act, default assessment, interest on outstanding tax, and potential criminal referral for intentional evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Payroll Reconciliation (EMP501) and Employees' Tax Certificates (IRP5/IT3(a))
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the annual cycle 1 March to 28/29 February, submission and employee certificate issue must be completed on or before 31 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest on unremitted PAYE, penalty up to 10% of unpaid amounts, and understatement penalty up to 200% in cases of deliberate concealment or gross negligence

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required where the company's public interest score (PIS) is 350 or greater. Companies with PIS between 100 and 349 must obtain an independent review unless the memorandum of incorporation, a shareholder agreement, or a court order specifically requires a full audit. A private company with PIS below 100 is normally exempt from audit and independent review unless required by the memorandum of incorporation or regulatory licensing conditions. PIS is computed from turnover, asset size, number of employees, and third-party liability exposure.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB is required for public-interest entities and larger companies. Private companies may apply IFRS for SMEs, or a recognised non-IFRS framework only where permissible under the Companies Act and the CIPC reporting requirements. Financial statements must present a true and fair view and include a directors' responsibility statement.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The CIPC annual return filing operates as the annual confirmation that the recorded shareholding and prescribed-officer details are current. Beneficial ownership particulars must be filed with CIPC within 30 days of any direct or indirect ownership change and must be promptly endorsed in the register of shareholders. There is no standalone recurring UBO annual declaration where no ownership changes have occurred, but the annual return must still be accompanied by confirmation of such unchanged records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders) including beneficial ownership particulars
Register of Directors and Prescribed Officers
Minute Book containing minutes of board and general shareholder meetings
Register of debentures and similar securities (if any)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (South African normal corporate income tax for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; 28% applied to earlier years of assessment)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to a marine insurance surveyor. The material rate-reducing provisions are: s11(a) general trade deductions for surveyor salaries, vessel/vehicle running costs, classification-society fees, professional indemnity insurance and overseas travel; s11(d)/s12C wear-and-tear and capital allowances (20% to 40% reducing-balance) on survey drones, ROVs, office equipment and vehicles; s11D research-and-development allowance at 150% of qualifying expenditure where proprietary hull-inspection software is developed in-house; s12B renewable-energy allowances (50/30/20) for solar-powered survey stations; and s12H learnership allowances. The graduated Small Business Corporation rate (7% to 21%) is available only where annual gross income is below ZAR 20 million and all shareholders are natural persons, which a compact (Pty) Ltd surveyor may satisfy.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory time limit on assessed losses under s20 of the Income Tax Act); however, for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023, an assessed loss may be set off against only 80% of taxable income in any given year pursuant to s20(1A).
